clues.title: Plate: long, white; red private, black public
text: Nepali licence plates are typically fairly long, with the most common design being white. Private vehicles use red plates, while public vehicles use black ones.

images.caption: Nepali plates: standard, black public and red private

clues.summary: Fairly long plates, most often white. Private vehicles use red plates and public vehicles black ones.

clues.title: Camera: low-quality, brownish, big blur on car
text: All of the road coverage in Nepal was taken with what’s commonly referred to as **“shitcam”**, which is a low-quality camera that can typically be recognised by the brownish colours and often, but not always, by a large circular blur covering the Street View car.
NOTE: Shitcam coverage is also very common in India and can rarely be found in Bangladesh and Sri Lanka.
clues.summary: All road coverage uses a low-quality camera: brownish colours and often, not always, a large round blur over the car. Very common in India, rare in Bangladesh and Sri Lanka.

clues.title: Driving side: left
text: Nepal drives on the** left side** of the road.
clues.summary: Traffic drives on the left.

clues.title: Language: Devanagari
text: Nepal uses the **Devanagari script**, which can be recognised by the line going through the top of each word and the straight vertical lines found in the majority of all letters.

NOTE: The characters ङ and especially ङ्ग are much more common in Nepali than in Hindi/Marathi. It is also quite common to find [native Devanagari numbers](https://maps.app.goo.gl/iZWe7Td5ovENJDEF7) on signage in Nepal, which is very rare in India.
clues.summary: Devanagari script: a line runs along the top of each word and most letters have straight vertical strokes. The letters ङ and ङ्ग are much more common than in Hindi or Marathi, and local-script numbers on signs are common, but very rare in India.

differs.how: Same script, but fewer ङ letters and few Devanagari numbers on signs

clues.title: Pole: square concrete, trident top
text: Nepal typically uses square concrete poles in the flat areas, and thin metallic poles in the mountainous regions. The poletops vary, but it is often some kind of trident.

The concrete pole with a [trident pole top and triangle supports](https://maps.app.goo.gl/ZpwKw2HMY3K4QkQy9) is unique to Nepal. Another common pole almost unique to Nepal is a concrete square pole with [2 vertical insulators](https://maps.app.goo.gl/RBVJCNrtq2enZDS47) on the sides with a wide gap between them. Other poles can often appear very similar to poles in India.
clues.summary: Square concrete poles on flat land and thin metal poles in the mountains, often with a trident top. Concrete with trident top and triangle supports is unique here, and a square concrete pole with two vertical insulators far apart is almost unique. Others can look like Indian poles.

differs.how: Other pole types look very similar to Indian ones

clues.title: Road lines: yellow dashed or solid edges
text: Nepal commonly uses **outer yellow road lines** that are either [dashed](https://maps.app.goo.gl/QEJcARP1NNPetPwS8) or [solid](https://maps.app.goo.gl/sAwmxo23B4o9Hc4m7), with dashed white lines in the middle of bigger roads. Solid outer yellows are very common in eastern Bagmati province.
clues.summary: Yellow edge lines, dashed or solid, with dashed white centre lines on bigger roads. Solid yellow edges are very common in the east of the central province.

clues.title: Bollard: black-white striped concrete, red top
text: Nepal mainly uses **black-and-white striped concrete bollards** that often have a **red marking** on the top. The amount of stripes vary from 3 to 5.
clues.summary: Black-and-white striped concrete bollards, often with a red mark on top. They have 3 to 5 stripes.

clues.title: Landscape: flat farmland south
text: You will see **flat agricultural areas** in the south as well as high altitude **mountain roads** in the northern half of Nepal.
clues.summary: Flat agricultural land in the south and high-altitude mountain roads in the north half.

clues.title: Houses: colourful blocks
text: Most buildings are either colorful blocky multi-story structures or small houses with painted concrete, red brick, or thatched looking walls, with either a tiled or tin roof. As part of the building facade, you will often spot [triangle shaped decorations](https://maps.app.goo.gl/YV9ysBvzpGBpQdwJ9).

images.caption: Colourful blocky houses in four shots; the circle magnifies the roof edge of the orange house

clues.summary: Colourful blocky multi-storey buildings or small houses with painted concrete, red brick or thatch-like walls and tile or tin roofs. Triangle-shaped decorations are often on the facade.

clues.title: Sign: black-and-white striped posts
text: Nepal uses black-and-white striped signposts.
NOTE: Within South and Southeast Asia, India, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Malaysia also use black-and-white striped signposts.
clues.summary: Black-and-white striped signposts. India, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Malaysia use them too.

clues.title: Landmark: white stupa, painted eyes
text: This type of **white-painted Buddhist stupa**, sometimes with painted eyes on the sides, are only found in Nepal.
clues.summary: A white-painted Buddhist stupa, sometimes with painted eyes on the sides, found only here.

clues.title: Addresses: district shown, often in English
text: Districts can show up on addresses, often in English as well.
clues.summary: Districts can appear in addresses, often in English too.

clues.title: Landscape: flat far south
text: The area in the far south close to the Indian border is almost completely flat, while the central and northern parts are very high altitude and very mountainous.
clues.summary: The far south near the Indian border is almost totally flat. The centre and north are very high and mountainous.

clues.title: Landscape: dry western hills, bare slopes
text: The western hills can be recognised by the **dry landscape**, with a lot of exposed hillsides lacking vegetation.
clues.summary: The western hills look dry, with many bare hillsides lacking vegetation.

clues.title: Plants: areca palms, thin trunk, small crown
text: **Areca Palms** can be recognised by their very thin trunk and a small crown. They are mainly found in the southeast.
clues.summary: Areca palms have a very thin trunk and a small crown. Mainly in the southeast.

clues.title: Plants: bright yellow canola fields
text: **Canola, **a crop with bright yellow flowers, is mostly found in a few southern pockets in the western half of Nepal.
clues.summary: Canola, a crop with bright yellow flowers, is mostly in a few southern pockets in the western half.

clues.title: Plants: chir pines, smooth crown, long needles
text: **Chir Pines**, which can be identified from their generally smooth-looking conical or spherical crowns with very long needles, are found everywhere in the mountains, but are much more common in the west, and near Kathmandu.
NOTE: The eastern region is generally greener than the west.
clues.summary: Chir pines have smooth cone or ball shaped crowns with very long needles. Found throughout the mountains but far more in the west and near the capital. The east is generally greener than the west.

clues.title: Plants: grass with white fluffy tips
text: Grass with white and fluffy-looking tips is most commonly found just southeast of Kathmandu.
While it can be found in most of the country, it usually won’t look as white and fluffy outside the dark red coloured region.
clues.summary: Grass with white, fluffy tips is most common just southeast of the capital. It is found in much of the country but looks less white outside the marked dark-red area.

clues.title: Plants: tall Japanese cedar
text: Japanese cedar trees, which are only found in far eastern Nepal, can typically be recognised by their significant height combined with their narrow, fluffy-looking crowns.
clues.summary: Japanese cedars grow only in the far east. They are very tall with narrow, fluffy-looking crowns.

clues.title: Plants: tea plantations, far east only
text: Tea Plantations are also only found in far eastern Nepal. Both in the mountains, and in the flat region.
clues.summary: Tea plantations are found only in the far east, both in the mountains and on the flat land.

clues.title: Roofs: rounded tiles, flat south and west
text: **Rounded roof tiles** are most common in the flat regions south of Kathmandu, but are also prevalent further west.
NOTE: Don’t mix this up with the [half-rounded tiles](https://maps.app.goo.gl/4WMe1LBb2TXwU1Za6), which are part of the hint below this.
clues.summary: Rounded roof tiles are most common on the flat land south of the capital and also widespread further west. Don't confuse them with the half-rounded tiles in the next tip.

clues.title: Roofs: organised tiles with small diamond bumps
text: West Bengal style roof tiles, which are more organised and have small **diamond shaped protrusions**, are most common in the far west flat region. This hint also works for the [half-rounded tiles](https://maps.app.goo.gl/4WMe1LBb2TXwU1Za6).
clues.summary: More orderly tiles with small diamond-shaped bumps, most common in the far western flat region. Also works for half-rounded tiles.

clues.title: Ground: neat grey square stone tiles
text: Flat **square shaped stone tiles** that are grey in colour are common south of Kathmandu, more specifically around Birgunj and Janakpur.
NOTE: Neat, square, stone tiles are not found in parts of India that tend to look similar to Nepal.
clues.summary: Flat, square, grey stone tiles are common south of the capital, around Birgunj and Janakpur. Parts of India that look similar to Nepal do not have such neat square tiles.

differs.how: Neat square stone tiles are not found in similar-looking parts

clues.title: Roofs: untidy rectangular tiles
text: Rectangular tiles that are** less organised** in shape and placement are common in western mountain towns, but can also be found towards the center of the country.
clues.summary: Rectangular tiles with messier shapes and placement are common in western mountain towns, and also towards the centre.

clues.title: Roofs: corrugated metal sheets
text: Roofs made from sheets of** corrugated metal** are most common between Birgunj and Janakpur.
clues.summary: Corrugated metal sheet roofs are most common between Birgunj and Janakpur.

clues.title: Roofs: railing along the sides, dark concrete
text: Roofs that have a **railing** along the sides of the roofs, usually made of dark concrete, are found in some parts of western Nepal. They are most common in the Tulsipur valley, where the railings sometimes have a [stair shape](https://maps.app.goo.gl/ikhV9mfvD98582v9A). The easternmost region where they’re found is the plains by Kawasoti. The westernmost regions often have lower quality “railings”, sometimes consisting of a few sticks.
clues.summary: Roofs with a railing along the sides, usually dark concrete, in parts of the west, most commonly in the Tulsipur valley where it is sometimes stair-shaped. The eastern limit is the plains near Kawasoti, and the far west has poorer rails, sometimes just sticks.

clues.title: Houses: gable ends with gold carved gods
text: Gable ends decorated by **carvings of gods**, goddesses, and other religious symbols, usually painted in a golden colour, are mostly around Kawasoti, west of Bharatpur.
clues.summary: Gable ends decorated with carved gods, goddesses and religious symbols, usually painted gold, mostly around Kawasoti, west of Bharatpur.

clues.title: Fences: stick fences of varying quality
text: Fences of varying build quality, made of mainly sticks, are most commonly found in the eastern plains of Nepal.
clues.summary: Fences made mostly of sticks, of varying quality, are most common in the eastern plains.

clues.title: Roofs: sheet metal
text: In the far east, you will mainly see roofs made of sheet metal with a triangular "window" just below the ridge of the roof, and an outwards sloping section below it.
clues.summary: In the far east: sheet metal roofs with a triangular window just below the ridge and an outward-sloping section underneath.

clues.title: Roofs: big metal hip roofs, small ridge bump
text: Large hip roofs made of sheet metal with a small protrusion just below the ridge are found around Biratnagar in the east.
clues.summary: Large hip roofs of sheet metal with a small protrusion just below the ridge, around Biratnagar in the east.

clues.title: Roofs: metal hip roofs, tiny ridge protrusion
text: Similar to the above hint, hip roofs made of sheet metal with an even smaller protruding piece of metal at the ridge are mainly found west of and around Biratnagar.
clues.summary: Like the previous one, but with an even smaller metal piece at the ridge, mainly west of and around Biratnagar.

clues.title: Mosques: only a few southern Muslim areas
text: Mosques are concentrated in a few Muslim majority spots in southern Nepal.
- In the east, just around Janakpur.
- In the east, just around Birgunj.
- In the west, just around Nepalgunj.
- In the east, around Biratnagar and west of the Koshi river.
clues.summary: Mosques cluster in a few Muslim-majority spots in the south: around Janakpur, around Birgunj, around Nepalgunj in the west, and around Biratnagar west of the Koshi river.

clues.title: Houses: small round clay huts, thatched roofs
text: Small** round clay huts** with **thatched roofs** are mainly found around Birgunj.
NOTE: These are also common just over the border in India.
clues.summary: Small round clay huts with thatched roofs are mainly around Birgunj. They are also common just across the border in India.

clues.title: Pole: cross attached near the top
text: Poles with a **cross** attached near the top are common in the east.
clues.summary: Poles with a cross attached near the top are common in the east.

clues.title: Pole: asymmetric crossbar with triangle on top
text: In Kathmandu, you’ll find poles with an asymmetrical crossbar, which has a triangular attachment on top of it, as well as a support bar below it.
clues.summary: In the capital, poles have an asymmetrical crossbar with a triangular attachment on top and a support bar below.

clues.title: Water tanks: green and black
text: While the most common water tank colours in Nepal are green and black, which are found everywhere, **yellow** ones are mainly found in the east.
clues.summary: Green and black water tanks are common everywhere. Yellow ones are mainly in the east.

clues.title: Google car: orange car
text: An orange google car can be found around:
- Nepalgunj in the west
- Madi, south of Bharatpur in the central south
- Biratnagar in the east
- Birtamod in the far east.
clues.summary: An orange Google car appears around Nepalgunj in the west, Madi south of Bharatpur, Biratnagar in the east, and Birtamod in the far east.

clues.title: Google car: orange car with blue ribbon on
text: An orange car with a blue ribbon on the front is found around Biratnagar.
clues.summary: An orange car with a blue ribbon on the front, around Biratnagar.

clues.title: Google car: blue car
text: A blue car is found around:
- Pokhara, under the Nepal label
- Birgunj, southwest of Kathmandu
- Malangawa, near the Indian border southeast of Kathmandu.
clues.summary: A blue car around Pokhara, Birgunj (southwest of the capital) and Malangawa (near the Indian border southeast of the capital).

clues.title: Google car: blue car with antenna
text: If the blue car has an antenna, you will be around Pokhara.
clues.summary: If the blue car has an antenna, you are around Pokhara.

clues.title: Google car: white car
text: A white car can be found in the following areas:
- Around Butwal, southwest of the Nepal label
- On the H10 going to Pokhara
- On the H04 east to Kathmandu
- On some roads near Kathmandu
- Northeast of Birgunj, southwest of Kathmandu
- From Janakpur to Lahan, southeast of Kathmandu
- Around Itahari, in the east.
clues.summary: A white car around Butwal, the H10 to Pokhara, the H04 east to the capital, some roads near the capital, northeast of Birgunj, from Janakpur to Lahan, and around Itahari in the east.

clues.title: Google car: car with black spoiler
text: A car with a black spoiler is found just around Janakpur, southeast of Kathmandu.
clues.summary: A car with a black spoiler, just around Janakpur, southeast of the capital.

clues.title: Google car: regular grey car
text: A regular grey car can be found around Kathmandu, and to the southeast, around Lahan.
clues.summary: A regular grey car around the capital and to the southeast around Lahan.

clues.title: Google car: blocky grey truck
text: A blocky grey truck can be found east of Birgunj and just south of Kathmandu.
clues.summary: A blocky grey truck east of Birgunj and just south of the capital.

clues.title: Google car: grey car with visible rear window
text: A grey car with a visible backlight can be found in the following areas:
- Around Pokhara, under the Nepal label
- Around Kathmandu
- North of Malangawa, near the Indian border southeast of Kathmandu
- East of Itahari, in the east.
clues.summary: A grey car with a visible backlight around Pokhara, around the capital, north of Malangawa near the Indian border, and east of Itahari in the east.

clues.title: Google car: red car, usually long antenna
text: A red car, that usually has a long antenna, can be found in Kathmandu, and north of Janakpur, which is southeast of Kathmandu.
clues.summary: A red car, usually with a long antenna, in the capital and north of Janakpur, southeast of the capital.

clues.title: Landscape: high hills with dark green
text: Some roads north of Siddhicharan, in eastern Nepal are unique due to the high elevation hills with dark green rhododendron bushes growing in abundance. The bushes have [red flowers](https://maps.app.goo.gl/ZyeniQ6umodMPa7h9) which can be hard to see.
clues.summary: Some roads north of Siddhicharan in the east have high hills with plenty of dark green rhododendron bushes. Their red flowers can be hard to see.

clues.title: Vegetation: foggy road, tall dark fir forest
text: This foggy and gloomy road hosts the only natural forest dominated by east himalayan fir. You can recognise it from all the tall dark trees present around the road. It is located just northwest of Bhimeshwor Municipality, east of Kathmandu.
clues.summary: A foggy, gloomy road with the only natural forest dominated by east Himalayan fir: tall dark trees all around. It is northwest of Bhimeshwor, east of the capital.

clues.title: Road: yellow-orange dirt, high-altitude oaks
text: This sketchy yellow/orange dirt road can be recognised from the high elevation landscape with the high elevation oaks. It can be found northeast of Phungling in far northeastern Nepal.
clues.summary: A rough yellow-orange dirt road in high-altitude land with mountain oaks, northeast of Phungling in the far northeast.

clues.title: Road: dirt track in a valley
text: This dirt track in a northwestbound valley can be recognised by the **snowcapped mountains** to the northwest. You can find it north of the Khaptad national park in western Nepal.
clues.summary: A dirt track in a valley heading northwest with snowcapped mountains ahead. North of a national park in the west.

clues.title: Coverage: trekker only in the northeast
text: Trekker coverage in Nepal is limited to the **northeast** of the country, in the general area southwest of Mount Everest.
clues.summary: Trekker coverage is limited to the northeast, southwest of Mount Everest.

clues.title: Vegetation: green forest in the south of the
text: **Green forests** and trees are found in the southern parts of the Nepalese trekker coverage.
clues.summary: Green forests and trees appear in the southern parts of the trekker coverage.

clues.title: Landscape: barren mountain trails in the north
text: **Barren mountain trails** are found in the northern parts of the coverage.
clues.summary: Barren mountain trails appear in the northern parts of the trekker coverage.

clues.title: Coverage: sunny trails at treeline
text: A lot of the coverage in the vicinity of Namche Bazar can be summarised as being sunny, with the trails going **close to the treeline**, meaning you will be either near the top of or just above a forest for most of this coverage. You will generally see barren or snowy mountains in some direction.
clues.summary: Around Namche Bazar the coverage is sunny, with trails near the treeline, so you are at the top of or just above a forest, with barren or snowy mountains somewhere in view.

clues.title: Coverage: largest, densest trekker village
text: Namche Bazar is by far the **largest** and **most densely populated** settlement with trekker coverage. There is also some coverage [looking down on the town](https://www.google.com/maps/@27.8056067,86.71193,2a,90y,112.78h,82.14t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1s9HNBGJ7FGOq9a4fOPyvWcg!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu).
clues.summary: Namche Bazar is by far the largest and most densely populated settlement with trekker coverage, with some coverage looking down on the town.

clues.title: Coverage: narrow street, big buildings
text: The southernmost trekker coverage is situated in the town of Lukla, which can be recognised by the narrow street with relatively large buildings, combined with the **extremely dark coverage**.
clues.summary: The southernmost trekker coverage is in Lukla: a narrow street with relatively large buildings and extremely dark coverage.

clues.title: Village: jagged mountain above, green roofs
text: Khumjung village, situated just north of Namche Bazar, can be recognised by the **jagged mountain** towering above the village. Almost every house in the village has a **green roof**.
Beware that there is a label for Khumjung further north, which is not close to the village.
clues.summary: Khumjung, just north of Namche Bazar, has a jagged mountain towering over it and almost every house has a green roof. A Khumjung label further north is not near the village.

clues.title: Village: fairly large, bright
text: Pangboche is a fairly large settlement with fairly bright coverage. The surrounding landscape mainly consists of **forested mountains** nearby and some taller mountains in the distance.
clues.summary: Pangboche is a fairly large settlement with fairly bright coverage, forested mountains nearby and taller mountains in the distance.

clues.title: Village: sparse, huge mountain close
text: Phorste is a fairly scarcely built settlement with a massive **recognizable mountain** close by. There are a lot of dead-looking trees surrounding the village.
clues.summary: Phorste is sparsely built with a massive, recognisable mountain nearby and many dead-looking trees around.

clues.title: Coverage: dark overcast forested valley
text: Around the southern tip of the Nepalese trekker coverage, you will get this **dark**, overcast coverage inside a forested valley.
clues.summary: Around the southern tip of the trekker coverage, dark, overcast coverage inside a forested valley.

clues.title: Coverage: overcast but brighter forest valley
text: North of Phakding you will get more overcast coverage in the same forest valley, however here the coverage is **far brighter**.
clues.summary: North of Phakding, more overcast coverage in the same forest valley, but much brighter.

clues.title: Coverage: sunny, bright forest valley
text: The coverage from Monjo up to Namche Bazar is also within the same valley, however here the coverage is mostly **sunny** and bright.
clues.summary: From Monjo up to Namche Bazar, in the same valley, mostly sunny and bright coverage.

clues.title: Valley: forested slopes
text: The valley by Thamu can be recognised by the generally forested mountainsides, combined with the **angle of the valley**, going northwest to southeast.
clues.summary: The valley by Thamu has generally forested mountainsides and runs northwest to southeast.

clues.title: Landscape: snowy, shining mountain range
text: Next to the village of Thame you can see this snowy, and **shining bright** mountain range.
clues.summary: Next to the village of Thame you see a snowy mountain range shining brightly.

clues.title: Landscape: semi-green valley
text: Northeast of Namche Bazar, you can find this **semi-green river valley** with clouds covering all mountains surrounding it.
clues.summary: Northeast of Namche Bazar, a semi-green river valley with clouds covering all the surrounding mountains.

clues.title: Landscape: cloud-blanketed peak
text: On a section north of Phorste, you get a view of the mountain Tobuche, covered in a **blanket of clouds**.
clues.summary: On a section north of Phorste you see Tobuche mountain covered in a blanket of clouds.

clues.title: Sky: small spotty clouds like chimney smoke
text: Further north, the cloud blanket is replaced by **small, spotty clouds** somewhat resembling smoke coming out of chimneys.
clues.summary: Further north the cloud blanket gives way to small, spotty clouds that look a bit like smoke from chimneys.

clues.title: Landscape: clear view of the peak
text: Even further north, the clouds disappear completely, and you get a **clear view** of the Tobuche peak.
clues.summary: Even further north the clouds disappear and the Tobuche peak is clearly visible.

clues.title: Landscape: small icy lake
text: Leaving Tobuche behind, you will find this small, **ice-covered lake**, right by Gokyo, with jagged mountains as a backdrop.
clues.summary: Past Tobuche, a small ice-covered lake right by Gokyo with jagged mountains behind.

clues.title: Landscape: barren land
text: North of the icy lake, you reach a barren landscape, with a trail going to the **north-north-west**.
clues.summary: North of the icy lake the land is barren, with a trail heading north-northwest.

clues.title: Valley: dried glacial valley, bright grey rocks
text: East of Gokyo, you reach this **dried out glacial valley**, with bright grey rocks as far as you can see.
NOTE: This valley can less commonly be seen from the trail [north of Gokyo](https://goo.gl/maps/pnV63nxPuKLv6bhd7).
clues.summary: East of Gokyo, a dried-out glacial valley with bright grey rocks as far as you can see. It is less commonly seen from the trail north of Gokyo.

clues.title: Landscape: red rugged mountainside next to
text: East of the glacial valley, you get to a somewhat **red-coloured**, rugged mountainside **right next to the trail**.
clues.summary: East of the glacial valley, a somewhat red, rugged mountainside right beside the trail.

clues.title: Valley: U-shaped, climbing steeply
text: Leaving the red mountainside behind, you enter a somewhat **U-shaped valley**, going firmly upwards.
clues.summary: After the red mountainside, a somewhat U-shaped valley going steadily upward.

clues.title: Landscape: spiky mountain range
text: Above the U-shaped valley, you get a view of this **spiky mountain range**. While there are some clouds around the peaks, they are mostly clearly visible.
clues.summary: Above the U-shaped valley, a spiky mountain range, mostly clearly visible with some clouds around the peaks.

clues.title: Landscape: crossing a glacier
text: As you lose sight of the spiky mountains, you cross over a **glacier**, which is the largest patch of snow covered ground with coverage in the country.
clues.summary: After losing sight of the spiky mountains you cross a glacier, the largest snow-covered patch with coverage in the country.

clues.title: Sky: many irregular clouds over peaks
text: The area east of the glacier can be recognised by the many **irregular clouds** spread across the sky and covering various mountain peaks.
clues.summary: East of the glacier, many irregular clouds spread across the sky and cover various peaks.

clues.title: Landscape: view of the peak from the east
text: Further along the trail, you get this stunning **view over Tobuche** from the eastern side. The mountains get increasingly covered in clouds to the west.
clues.summary: Further along, a view over Tobuche from the east. Mountains get more cloud-covered to the west.

clues.title: Valley: wide high-altitude river valley
text: Closing in on the final trek toward Everest, you get a view of this wide, **high-altitude river valley**.
clues.summary: Near the final stretch toward Everest, a wide, high-altitude river valley.

clues.title: Trail: overcast mountainside, trees
text: Slightly east of Namche Bazar, you can find this very overcast trail following the mountainside. There are still some trees around, and the trail is noticeably **higher** above the valley than other overcast sections with trees.
clues.summary: Slightly east of Namche Bazar, a very overcast trail along the mountainside with some trees, noticeably higher above the valley than other overcast tree sections.

clues.title: Trail: overcast forest, bright sandy dirt
text: East of the POI called ‘Deboche’, you get this very **overcast forest coverage**. The dirt here is very bright and sandy, which can help differentiate it from the southern trail.
clues.summary: East of the place called Deboche, very overcast forest coverage. The dirt is very bright and sandy, unlike the southern trail.

clues.title: Trail: massive mountains, hazy sun
text: You can recognise the trail between Pangboche and Dingboche by the massive mountains, combined with the sun looking somewhat **hazy**.
clues.summary: The trail between Pangboche and Dingboche has massive mountains and a somewhat hazy sun.

clues.title: Valley: high-altitude, very low clouds
text: North of Dingboche, you reach a high-altitude valley with very **low clouds** covering the sky and most of the surrounding mountains.
clues.summary: North of Dingboche, a high-altitude valley with very low clouds over the sky and most surrounding mountains.

clues.title: Landscape: completely barren
text: Closing in on Everest, you get this completely barren landscape, with the trail going to the **north-north-east**.
clues.summary: Closing in on Everest the landscape is completely barren, with the trail heading north-northeast.

clues.title: Coverage: end of trail
text: Reaching the endpoint of the coverage, you finally get a stunning view of the world's tallest mountain, **Mount Everest**.
clues.summary: At the end of the coverage you finally get a clear view of Mount Everest, the world's tallest mountain.
